sections.title: Tree and leaves
sections.text: Terminalia paniculata is a large deciduous tree native to peninsular India, reported to reach about 33 m. Its simple, oblong leaves are usually 9–18 × 4.5–7 cm; lower leaves may be opposite and upper leaves alternate. The plate shows the broad leaves and tree habit.

sections.title: Flowers and winged fruit
sections.text: Small pale flowers are borne on branched spikes. The fruit is a brownish-red, one-seeded samara with three unequal wings, the central wing largest. The plate's narrow flower spike and asymmetric winged fruit agree with this description.

sections.title: Food and uses
sections.text: The tree is reported as a useful timber species. The sources consulted do not establish whether its fruit is edible or toxic to people.
